issues.summary: Over-broad reuse of lExpression makes TypeOf and AddressOf accept invalid operands (literals, calls under AddressOf, bang access under AddressOf, implicit-With under AddressOf).
issues.resolution: Introduced two new rules: procedureReference (used by addressOfExpr) restricts AddressOf operands to dotted (IDENTIFIER|TYPED_IDENTIFIER|ME).memberName chains - no calls, bang, implicit-With, or literals. referenceExpression (used by typeOfExpr) is an l-expression-shaped rule that excludes literal/special-constant primaries. Updated existing AddressOf tests to access addressOfExpr.procedureReference() instead of .lExpression().

issues.summary: No negative tests cover invalid TypeOf/AddressOf forms.
issues.resolution: Added TypeOf_LiteralOperand_FailsToParse (3 cases: literal int, string, date) and AddressOf_NonProcedureReference_FailsToParse (4 cases: call, bang, implicit-With, literal). Each asserts InvalidOperationException via the ThrowingErrorListener.

issues.summary: procedureReference accepted bare `AddressOf Me`. Me is the class instance, not a procedure pointer, so the form is a spec violation.
issues.resolution: Split procedureReference into two alternatives: `(IDENTIFIER|TYPED_IDENTIFIER) (DOT memberName)*` (covers all non-Me forms, optionally qualified) and `ME (DOT memberName)+` (Me must be followed by at least one member). Bare `Me` no longer parses as a procedure reference. Inlined procedureRefHead into procedureReference. Added `AddressOf Me` to the AddressOf_NonProcedureReference_FailsToParse theory.
